properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured, corrected the same day): a triage recorded "should reflow2 serve a design in operations?" as OPEN, with "beside the design" and "nothing new" as options, although the answer was on the record. It is in docs/vision.md since the first commit, and in the graph in accepted pieces: req:coherence ("any phase"), req:design-and-implementation-stay-coherent-both-ways (feedback flows back), and req:epochs-can-be-planned (capability delivered in small frequent increments, so development and operations run at the same time). No single node ties them together as the scope. The brainstorm skill sends the agent to search for related IDEAS, never for the accepted intent that may already answer the question
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, on Anthony's challenge during the triage of art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28.

① OBSERVED. The agent recorded dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-design-in-operations-where-incidents-feed-the-design as "OPEN — should reflow2 serve a design IN OPERATIONS ... as a first-class use". Its options included (b) incidents live beside the design and (d) nothing new. It drew RISKS to the fewer-things brainstorm, and wrote that option (a) "is how a design brain becomes a mediocre maintenance system". This happened although the same record quoted the owner saying "Reflow2 encompasses the full lifecycle of a project, so this use case is included in reflow2", and cited req:coherence as an argument FOR.

Anthony, verbatim: "how is the question 'should reflow2 serve a design that is already in operations?' not already answered? I've designed reflow2 from the beginning to be the complete lifecycle from concept to operations/fielding. One of the core principles of reflow2 is that design doesn't drift from implementation. We've even compared this to UAF, which also captures the full life-cycle ... the answer, in my mind, is very clearly yes." He added that many projects never finish integrating: under continuous delivery there is "a near continuous cycle to iterative deployment, testing, feedback, operations that sticks around for years", and the B-52, first flown 15 April 1952, is being extended to fly into the 2050s and 2060s.

EXPECTED: the record states the settled scope and asks only HOW. NOT AFFECTED: the operations ideas and findings the same triage recorded (O-17 to O-24, F-30 to F-36). They are how-questions and stay valid.

② PRECEDENT. search_design on the raw question returned the new record itself and its child ideas, and no settled node that states the scope. The search made when the record was written ("operations phase troubleshooting deployment lifecycle incident field use after build") returned req:coherence as its 5th hit.

③ CANDIDATES.
(A) THE GRAPH HOLDS THE SCOPE TOO THINLY TO BE FOUND. The founding statement lives in a document the design does not register.
(B) THE SKILL NEVER ASKS "IS THIS ALREADY ANSWERED?". The brainstorm skill searches for near-duplicate and related ideas, and no step checks accepted intent or the north star before a question is framed as open.
(C) SAME-DAY PRIMING. Two records written hours earlier framed the frame: the core-identity brainstorm, quoting the identity as "a person designs without knowing systems engineering", and the persona decision, "reflow2 keeps the design, a host keeps the rest". The agent carried both over by analogy.
(D) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG. The design states the scope plainly and the agent skipped it.

④ WHAT SEPARATES THEM. D predicts an accepted node whose text names operations as in scope. A predicts none, and a document elsewhere that does. B predicts no instruction in the brainstorm skill to check accepted intent. C predicts the record's own text leaning on the two same-day records.

⑤ RESULTS.
· A scan of every Requirement, Decision, DesignRule, Project and Constraint in the export found no accepted node that says "concept to operations", "full lifecycle", "fielding" or "sustainment" as reflow2's scope. Those phrases occur only in proposed ideas (lifecycle-dimensions, what-drives-a-capability-up-the-ladder). req:coherence (accepted, critical) says only "Design stays coherent across its lifecycle. When anything changes in any phase, the ripples are found and surfaced." req:design-and-implementation-stay-coherent-both-ways (accepted 2026-09-25) states the feedback principle, not the phases. proj:reflow2 carries no description.
· The repository states the scope plainly and has since the first commit (7d96ee6, 2026-07-17):
  - docs/vision.md is titled "Vision — one coherent graph from concept to operations". It names build → operate as a transition where programs break, lists "concept, design, build, test, production, O&M", says "The schema spans P0–P5, so concept and operations live in the same graph", and defines good as "Someone with only an idea is guided — by questions — from concept to operations without needing to know systems engineering."
  - README.md and AGENTS.md repeat "the entire lifecycle — concept → operations — in one graph".
  - docs/vision.md is NOT registered as an Artifact, so no DOCUMENTS edge reaches req:coherence from it. The 10 capabilities that satisfy req:coherence are all change machinery (change, detect, heal, propagate, loop-status, ...). None is operations-phase.
· The brainstorm skill's search steps are about duplicates and relations ("Judge the near-matches you already have. Do not run a fresh sweep"). No step asks whether accepted intent already answers the question.
· The record's own text cites the persona decision as the model for option (c) and links RISKS to the fewer-things brainstorm.
⇒ D REFUTED: nothing in the graph says it plainly. A, B and C all HOLD. A and B are the cause and C was the trigger: a thin line in the graph plus a skill that never looks for an answer let a same-day analogy frame a settled principle as open. The core-identity brainstorm quoted the identity one clause short. The vision's sentence ends "from concept to operations".

⑥ CLASS: a founding principle held in a document the design does not register, and in the graph only as a terse line, can be re-framed as an open question by any session that reads the graph and not the document. Nothing in the brainstorm path, and no detector, notices an exploratory Decision whose options contradict accepted intent. The class fix is twofold: the scope stated in the graph as intent, and the brainstorm skill told to look for the answer before framing the question. Rewording this one record fixes only the instance.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE: no code or skill text was changed. A test pinning the class would assert two things. Every sentence of the north star that states scope is reachable from an accepted Requirement, through its text or a DOCUMENTS edge. The brainstorm skill carries a step that searches accepted intent before an OPEN question is written.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: how many other exploratory Decisions frame settled intent as open (no census taken); whether the P0–P5 phase span the vision promises exists in today's schema (not checked).

CORRECTION, 2026-09-28, LATER THE SAME DAY, on Anthony's word: "one of the very reasons that I created epochs/increments into reflow2 was because many designs continue development and operations simultaneously in sort of an iterative or incremental deployment of capabilities. That is also in the reflow2 graph."

Measured, and he is right. Candidate (A) as written above overstates how thin the graph is. The graph holds the concurrent development-and-operations model in accepted intent:
· req:epochs-can-be-planned (accepted, 2026-07-28): two paired views, "increments in TIME" and "increments in CAPABILITY — what each small, frequent release adds, the release-fast-in-small-increments practice now common in industry". The roadmap is a satisfaction schedule across increments.
· req:plans-move-honestly and req:graph-indexes-snapshots (accepted): "what didn't we achieve that we were supposed to in increment 10?".
· Readiness gating (dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement, ver:readiness-gating): a demonstrator and a fielded increment demand different readiness of the same part.
· The as-fielded reconcile (cap:reconcile-deployed): releases deployed to environments, checked against what is observed running.
So the graph did not hold the scope as "one line". It holds it in several accepted pieces, and what it lacks is one statement tying them together as the reason: development and operations run at once, increment by increment.

REVISED READING OF ⑤: (A) is QUALIFIED, not held. The pieces were findable, and the umbrella's own search could have reached req:epochs-can-be-planned. (B) holds and is the larger cause: no step in the brainstorm skill asks whether accepted intent already answers the question. (C) holds as the trigger. The class statement in ⑥ stands, with its first half narrowed: what is missing is one node that ties the scope together, not the scope itself.
